program: Volunteer mental health access and community service
priceScope: Conditional FY2024 full annual cost against a current partial counseling channel; not measured whole-portfolio or marginal-gift effectiveness.

what: Spark connects Colorado residents facing care barriers to volunteer counseling and partner referrals, with up to ten free sessions.
It retains independent EIN84-0782124 as a Project Helping subsidiary and also operates other volunteer and senior/community programs.
The numerical reference uses an observed connection envelope, not verified unique completed therapy or parent-wide outcomes.
strengths: Current mental health access, licensed volunteers and recipient-specific giving route are identified.
Original three-year full annual recipient costs exclude parent-wide totals and avoid adding netted costs twice.
Health and signed resources include participation, alternative care and volunteer opportunity costs instead of free-service retail value.
reservations: Six thousand annual connections can include referrals; household uniqueness, clinical completion and causal effects remain judgments.
Current undated service counters are paired with FY2024 expense only as a conditional capacity reference, not measured FY2024 productivity.
Full costs cover senior, disaster and other work whose benefits remain unknown; neither community-support expense nor $75 session promotion is counseling marginal cost.

sections.what: The current program offers individual, couples and family counseling, host-site services and support groups. Up to ten sessions is a ceiling, not completed dose; the roughly three-week wait and partner referrals limit direct service assumptions. It does not provide crisis, inpatient or medication treatment.
sections.monitoring: Request unique annual direct patients, completed session distributions, referral-only clients, Denver beneficiary counts and controlled outcomes. Track current volunteer capacity and whether added gifts change access rather than replacing insurance or other providers.
sections.qualitative: Statewide staff and partner coverage do not establish Denver share. Medicaid, insurance, public clinics and other community providers remain alternatives. Parent Project Helping impact is excluded; clinical and household additionality are not established by testimonials.
sections.cost: FY2024 full annual cost is $2,111,453; netted event, gaming and inventory expenses are blank. Current 6,000+ annual connections are conservatively entered as 6,000, with judged 90% household uniqueness, 40% suitable completion, 40% additionality, 30% clinical response, .02 utility for half a year and 50% Denver share. These are not observed QALY coefficients. Changed households receive judged $100 after-tax/benefit/work-cost resources and $30 actual otherwise-paid copay avoidance, not retail therapy value; positive gains receive a 50% overlap adjustment. Full $10 access cost and process harm apply to every connected household. Distinct providers lose the full $30 actual copay per changed household. Volunteer opportunity loss is separately judged $30 per completed-service recipient, borne by volunteers rather than patients or providers, independent of benefit success. This does not duplicate the copay counterparty. Community-support $1,722,291 is only a mixed-program cost sensitivity; unmeasured other-program benefits are unknown, not zero.
sections.funding: Own homepage directs donors to this recipient’s ColoradoGives profile, which identifies the independent legal subsidiary. No transaction was made. The $75 session illustration and current high demand are not verified incremental capacity or full marginal cost; parent management and transfer scope remain uncertain.

model.costScope: Observed FY2024 independent-recipient full annual expense against a partial current counseling access channel. Parent totals not added; no allocated therapy or next-gift cost is claimed.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .5 share inside ten-county Denver CBSA19740; statewide coverage and other Colorado staff prevent an all-Denver assumption.
model.formula: Clinical health = (N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted duration − all-connected process harm) × Denver share. Household gains and full access costs are jointly logged; distinct provider loss and completed-service volunteer opportunity loss are retained with geography once. Price = 10 × C / combined equivalents.
model.counterfactual: Insurance, Medicaid, public and partner providers, other volunteer counselors and untreated care barriers without Spark. Completion and additionality are distinct hypotheses.
model.attribution: b=.4 causal additionality, completion=.4 and response=.3 are independent judgments, not a local trial or all connected clients receiving therapy.
model.uncertainty: Current unique clinical dose, effect utility/duration, donor capacity, geography, household resources, volunteer displacement and parent support are not measured. Finite, null, adverse and cost-boundary cases expose uncertainty.
model.nativeOutcomes: Current own mental wellness page states 6,000+ people connected annually, including partner referrals, and up to ten free sessions. Neither is a unique completed-patient outcome. Whole Spark volunteers/hours/projects and parent impact are excluded from clinical N.
